title: AM titanium alloys: process-structure-property review
text: Additive manufacturing of Ti-6Al-4V via laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) produces acicular alpha-prime martensite in the as-built condition, resulting in high strength (>1000 MPa UTS) but limited ductility (<10% elongation). Post-build annealing at 650-800°C transforms the martensitic microstructure to a lamellar alpha+beta morphology, restoring ductility while retaining strength levels above wrought Grade 5 (950 MPa). Key process parameters include laser power (200-400W), scan speed (800-1200 mm/s), and layer thickness (20-60 μm).

findings.summary: As-built LPBF Ti-6Al-4V achieves UTS >1000 MPa with alpha-prime martensite microstructure
Annealing at 650-800°C restores ductility by transforming martensite to lamellar alpha+beta

text_units.content: Ti-6Al-4V is the workhorse alloy for aerospace AM, comprising ~50% of all titanium AM parts produced globally.
The beta transus for Ti-6Al-4V is approximately 995°C. Processing below this temperature retains primary alpha, while above it produces fully martensitic or Widmanstätten structures on rapid cooling.

title: Inconel 718 AM: microstructure and mechanical properties
text: IN718 produced via LPBF exhibits columnar dendritic solidification with Nb segregation to interdendritic regions. As-built UTS typically reaches 1100-1200 MPa with 12-18% elongation. The standard two-step aging treatment (720°C/8h + 620°C/8h) precipitates gamma-prime and gamma-double-prime phases, increasing UTS to 1350-1450 MPa. Fatigue properties of AM IN718 remain a concern due to porosity and surface roughness effects.

findings.summary: AM IN718 requires double aging to achieve full precipitation strengthening
Porosity and surface roughness degrade fatigue life in as-built AM IN718

text_units.content: IN718 is a precipitation-hardenable nickel-chromium superalloy widely used in gas turbine and aerospace applications up to 650°C service temperature.
The gamma-prime [Ni3(Al,Ti)] and gamma-double-prime [Ni3Nb] precipitates provide the primary strengthening mechanism in aged IN718.
